name: Tselinny Center of Contemporary Culture
watch: Founder's wealth partly oil and gas; he was convicted and surrendered assets to the state.
why_flagged: Founder's wealth partly oil and gas; he was convicted and surrendered assets to the state.
records_note: Tselinny names its patrons by tier undated and lists an advisory board, but posts no annual report, accounts or governing board.

name: Kaesong Koryo Museum
watch: Hall 3 is usually closed to foreigners. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: State-run museum in Kaesong with over 1,000 Koryo-dynasty artefacts in four halls and an open-air stone collection; 20,000 m², 12 main buildings.
records_note: A North Korean state museum; searches found no website, report, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Sinchon Museum of American War Atrocities
watch: Rebuilt on a new site in July 2015. The Government of North Korea is blocked under US Executive Order 13722.
why_flagged: Memorial to the 1950 Sinchon massacre. The museum claims over 35,000 deaths and blames US forces; South Korean research finds anti-communist vigilantes and secret police carried out killings.
records_note: A North Korean state museum; no official website, report, accounts, donor list or board turned up.

name: Zachęta National Gallery of Art
watch: PKN Orlen is a fossil-fuel funder.
why_flagged: PKN Orlen is a fossil-fuel funder.
records_note: The gallery posts annual reports from 2011 to 2024 and yearly financial statements in its public bulletin; its partner page names ORLEN, but no board.

name: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
watch: Funded by Qatar Museums, a Gulf state body under labour critique.
why_flagged: Funded by Qatar Museums, a Gulf state body under labour critique.
records_note: Mathaf has no records of its own; its parent Qatar Museums posts no reports, accounts or sponsor names but lists eight trustees.

name: Museum of Islamic Art
records_note: The Museum of Islamic Art has no records of its own; parent Qatar Museums posts no reports, accounts or sponsors but lists eight trustees.

name: Victoria Gallery
watch: Sister institution of V-A-C ('Victoria — the Art of being Contemporary'); second site Victoria Underground since 2020.
why_flagged: Sister institution of V-A-C ('Victoria — the Art of being Contemporary'); second site Victoria Underground since 2020.
records_note: The gallery posts no annual report, accounts, partner list or board; its About page names founder Leonid Mikhelson and three managers.

name: New Holland Island
watch: Restoration and construction suspended June 2022; Fontanka links the stop to the EU freeze of Abramovich's assets in mid-March 2022; the project refused comment.
why_flagged: Restoration and construction suspended June 2022; Fontanka links the stop to the EU freeze of Abramovich's assets in mid-March 2022; the project refused comment.
records_note: The site posts no reports, accounts, sponsor list or board; its project page names Millhouse and the Iris Foundation as builders and creative partners.

name: PRO ARTE Foundation
watch: Vladimir Potanin is on the UK list (June 2022) and the US list (Dec 2022). PRO ARTE has run his foundation's grant competitions since 2016.
why_flagged: St Petersburg charitable foundation. Its 2025 report lists programme backers: the city's Committees for Culture and Social Policy, Friends of BDT Foundation and the Vladimir Potanin Foundation.
records_note: The foundation posts reports and audits for 2023 to 2025, names its five-member board, and its 2025 report lists backers including the Potanin Foundation.

name: State Hermitage Museum
watch: Hermitage Amsterdam cut ties on 3 March 2022. Canada sanctioned director Piotrovsky in 2023 and the EU listed him on 23 April 2026.
why_flagged: Its 2025 sponsor list includes VTB, Sberbank, Gazprom, Rosneft, Gazprom Neft and the Gazprombank foundation, plus Vladimir Potanin and his foundation. Potanin chairs the Board of Trustees.
records_note: The Hermitage posts yearly reports for 2009 to 2018 and a sponsor list by year (2022 seen); its reports name a board of trustees.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2011-05: An AP report in Stratfor's emails says Russia froze art loans to US museums after a US court backed Chabad's claim to the Schneerson library. Piotrovsky said Moscow would not permit US shows. (Stratfor emails (AP item))

name: State Russian Museum
watch: Vladimir Gusev (director since 1988) moved to president in Feb 2023; Deputy Culture Minister Alla Manilova appointed director 25 Apr 2023. 3.61m visits in 2024 per TAN ranking (via search).
why_flagged: Vladimir Gusev (director since 1988) moved to president in Feb 2023; Deputy Culture Minister Alla Manilova appointed director 25 Apr 2023. 3.61m visits in 2024 per TAN ranking (via search).
records_note: The museum posts no annual report or accounts and no board; its partners page names VTB in text and shows other partners only as logos.

name: Vyksa Festival (Art-Ovrag)
watch: Founded 2011 as Art-Ovrag, renamed 2020; OMK makes steel pipes for the oil and gas sector.
why_flagged: Founded 2011 as Art-Ovrag, renamed 2020; OMK makes steel pipes for the oil and gas sector.
records_note: The OMK-Uchastie fund behind the festival posts annual reports for 2019 to 2025 and spending reports, and names its partners, but no board.
